messages.subject: Vector dimensionality issue
parts:
Dear Stan list,

I ran into a vector dimensionality issue when trying to fit a multivariate regression-based model in Stan.  Specifically, I get the following error message:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::multi_normal_log(i): Size of random variableSize of random variable (2) and size of location parameter (3) must match in size
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.
Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

I am confused as to why this is happening, since the location parameter (mu0) which is fed into the multi_normal_log() function is, I understand, of the same dimension K as the variable x[n].  (In my particular simulation, K=2).

Any help would be greatly appreciated.  I have included my code below.  If there is any additional information I can provide, please let me know.

Thank you in advance; this list has been an incredibly useful resource for me in these past few months for learning Stan and resolving Stan-related issues!

Best,
Nik



data {

real<lower=0,upper=1> Pi;
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=0> N_inc;
int<lower=0> K;
matrix[N_inc, K] x;
int<lower=0,upper=1> w[N_inc];
int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N_inc];
// hyperparameter data
int<lower=0> hyp_p_a;
int<lower=0> hyp_p_b;
row_vector[K] hyp_mu;
cov_matrix[K] hyp_mu_sig;
row_vector[K+1] hyp_b;
cov_matrix[K+1] hyp_b_sig;
real hyp_Wishart_nu;
cov_matrix[K] hyp_Wishart_Sigma;
}

transformed data{
matrix[N_inc, K+1] xStar;

for(i in 1:N_inc) for(j in 2:(K+1)){
xStar[i, j] <- x[i, j-1];
}
for(i in 1:N_inc){
xStar[i,1] <- 1;
}
}


parameters{

// ASSIGNMENT MECHANISM PARAMETER
real<lower=0,upper=1> p;

// COVARIATE PARAMETERS
vector[K] mu0;
vector[K] mu1;
cov_matrix[K] sig0;
cov_matrix[K] sig1;

// POTENTIAL OUTCOMES GLM MODEL PARAMETERS
vector[K] b0;
vector[K] b1;

}

transformed parameters{
matrix[K+1, K+1] sig0star;
matrix[K+1,K +1] sig1star;
vector[K+1] mu0Star;
vector[K+1] mu1Star;
for(j in 1:(K+1)){
sig0star[1,j] <- 0;
}
for(j in 1:(K+1)){
sig1star[1,j] <- 0;
}
for(i in 1:(K+1)){
sig0star[i,1] <- 0;
}
for(i in 1:(K+1)){
sig1star[i,1] <- 0;
}
for(i in 2:(K+1)) for(j in 2:(K+1)){
sig0star[i, j] <- sig0[i-1, j-1];
}
for(i in 2:(K+1)) for(j in 2:(K+1)){
sig1star[i, j] <- sig1[i-1, j-1];
}

mu0Star[1] <- 1;
for(i in 2:(K+1)){
mu0Star[i] <- mu0[i-1];
}

mu1Star[1] <- 1;
for(i in 2:(K+1)){
mu1Star[i] <- mu1[i-1];
}

}


model{
// TEMP VECTORS OF LOG COMPONENT DENSITIES
real log_p_vec[N_inc];
real log_p_notSampled;
// PRIORS
p ~ beta(hyp_p_a, hyp_p_b);

mu0 ~ multi_normal(hyp_mu', hyp_mu_sig);
mu1 ~ multi_normal(hyp_mu', hyp_mu_sig);

sig0 ~ inv_wishart(hyp_Wishart_nu, hyp_Wishart_Sigma);
sig1 ~ inv_wishart(hyp_Wishart_nu, hyp_Wishart_Sigma);

b0 ~ multi_normal(hyp_b', hyp_b_sig);
b1 ~ multi_normal(hyp_b', hyp_b_sig);
// COMPUTING SAMPLED PART OF LOG-LIKELIHOOD
for(n in 1:N_inc){
log_p_vec[n] <-  w[n]*y[n]*log(Phi(xStar[n]*b1)+exp(-16))
+ w[n]*(1-y[n])*log(1-Phi(xStar[n]*b1)+exp(-16))
+ (1-w[n])*y[n]*log(Phi(xStar[n]*b0)+exp(-16))
+ (1-w[n])*(1-y[n])*log(1-Phi(xStar[n]*b0)+exp(-16))
+ (1-w[n])*log(1-p)
+ w[n]*log(p)
+ (1-w[n])*multi_normal_log(x[n]',mu0,sig0)
+ w[n]*multi_normal_log(x[n]',mu1,sig1);
}
// COPMUTING NON-SAMPLED PART
log_p_notSampled <- (N-N_inc) *
   log( 1 - (1-p)*Phi(mu1Star'*b1/sqrt(1+b1'*sig1star*b1)+exp(-16)) -
        p*Phi(mu0Star'*b0/sqrt(1+b0'*sig0star*b0)+exp(-16)) );
// SUM LOG-PROBABILITIES   
lp__ <- lp__ + sum(log_p_vec) + log_p_notSampled;

}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vector dimensionality issue
parts:
We really really need to get line numbers into our
error output! It's a high-priority to-do item on my
plate.

I'd recommend the sections on recommended univariate
and multivariate priors in the regression chapter of our manual.
We don't need to stick to Wisharts because we can handle
non-conjugate priors.

There are also more arithmetically stable ways to do what you're
doing here. Always use log1m(x) instead of log(1-x).

Is the weighting really linear like that on the log scale
with the (1 - w[n])? It's not giving you a mixture.

We've deprecated manipulating lp__ directly in favor of
increment_log_prob. And that vectorizes itself more efficiently
than all those binary + operations, so the clearer and more
efficient form of

...
...
// SUM LOG-PROBABILITIES
lp__ <- lp__ + sum(log_p_vec) + ...



is:

increment_log_prob(w[n] * y[n] * log(Phi(xStar[n] * b1) + exp(-16));
...


- Bob

and multivariate priors in the regression chapter of our manual.
We don't need to stick to Wisharts because we can handle
non-conjugate priors.

There are also more arithmetically stable ways to do what you're
doing here.  Always use log1m(x) instead of log(1-x).  

Is the weighting really linear like that on the log scale
with the (1 - w[n])?  It's not giving you a mixture.  

We've deprecated manipulating lp__ directly in favor of
increment_log_prob.  And that vectorizes itself more efficiently
than all those binary + operations, so the clearer and more
efficient form of

log_p_vec[n] <-  w[n]*y[n]*log(Phi(xStar[n]*b1)+exp(-16))
+ w[n]*(1-y[n])*log(1-Phi(xStar[n]*b1)+exp(-16))
+ (1-w[n])*y[n]*log(Phi(xStar[n]*b0)+exp(-16))
+ (1-w[n])*(1-y[n])*log(1-Phi(xStar[n]*b0)+exp(-16))
...
...
// SUM LOG-PROBABILITIES          
lp__ <- lp__ + sum(log_p_vec) + ...



is:

increment_log_prob(w[n] * y[n] * log(Phi(xStar[n] * b1) + exp(-16));
...


- Bob
